content.title: What is the Two Pointer Technique?
content.description: The Two Pointer technique uses two indices that move through an array or string to solve problems efficiently without repeatedly traversing the same elements.

content.content: The Two Pointer Technique is a powerful optimization strategy used in arrays, strings, linked lists, and sorting problems. Instead of using nested loops, two pointers work together to reduce unnecessary computations and improve efficiency.

content.title: Why Learn Two Pointers?
content.content: Many interview problems that initially appear to require O(n²) solutions can often be optimized to O(n) using Two Pointers.
Two Pointer techniques are commonly used when dealing with sorted arrays, pair finding problems, palindrome checking, partitioning, and optimization tasks involving contiguous data.

items.question: Pair Sum Problems
items.answer: Find two numbers whose sum equals a target value.

items.question: Palindrome Checking
items.answer: Compare characters from both ends moving inward.

content.content: One of the most popular Two Pointer problems is finding two elements whose sum equals a target value in a sorted array.

content.title: Pair Sum Workflow
steps: If sum equals target, return answer
If sum is smaller, move left pointer
If sum is larger, move right pointer

content.content: The Sliding Window Technique is a specialized form of Two Pointer approach used for processing contiguous segments of arrays or strings. Instead of recalculating every subarray, a window expands and shrinks dynamically.

content.title: Key Idea
content.description: Maintain a window of elements and update the result by adding and removing elements as the window moves.

content.content: Fixed-size Sliding Window is used when the window length remains constant. This is useful for finding maximum sums, averages, or frequencies within a fixed range.

content.title: Maximum Sum Subarray of Size K

content.content: Variable-size Sliding Window is used when the window expands and shrinks dynamically according to a condition. This technique is commonly used for longest substring and minimum window problems.

content.title: Variable Window Workflow
steps: Expand window by moving right pointer

content.title: Interview Pattern
content.content: Whenever a problem mentions contiguous subarrays, substrings, longest segment, minimum window, or maximum window, think about Sliding Window.

content.title: Security Camera Window
content.content: Imagine a security camera monitoring only a portion of a road at a time. As the camera moves, old vehicles leave the frame while new vehicles enter. This is exactly how a Sliding Window works.

items.question: What is the biggest Sliding Window mistake?
items.answer: Recalculating the entire window instead of updating incrementally.

items.question: When should Sliding Window not be used?
items.answer: When the problem does not involve contiguous elements.

items.question: Why do pointers get stuck?
items.answer: Because one pointer is not updated correctly inside loops.

content.title: Interview Insight
content.description: If you see words like contiguous, longest, shortest, maximum length, minimum window, substring, or subarray, immediately think about Sliding Window.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Sliding Window is a specialized Two Pointer technique.
Pair Sum problems often use Two Pointers.
Subarray and substring problems often use Sliding Window.
Most optimized solutions run in O(n).
These techniques are among the most frequently asked interview topics.
